items.log_text: Bark-tanned dog hide, slightly damp. Worked tallow in with both palms, grain side first. Let it absorb for an hour. Then staked and slicked the grain with the bone slicker — an old rib bone, smoothed on sandstone. The surface firms up and takes a mild sheen.

No tallow to spare. Used rendered cooking fat — less clean but the fat content is similar. A bottle shard for slicking. The glass edge burnishes finer than bone if kept moving. Leather came out close to the bone-slicked batch.

Willow-tanned hide requires more fat liquor — the tannin is lighter and the leather drinks more. Applied two coats of tallow with a day between. Final slicking took the grain down flat and even. Softer hand than the oak-tanned batch.

Tried bone marrow oil — rendered from cracked long bones. Smells strong. Works into the leather differently: faster penetration, slicker surface immediately. The bone slicker barely needed force. Finished leather is supple. Will use marrow oil when tallow is low.

Brain-tanned hide does not need heavy currying — the oils are already set. Light tallow rub and a smooth river stone for burnishing. The surface is already soft; the stone just brings up a faint gloss. More grooming than work.

Thick oak-tanned panel — stiff even after fatiquoring. Needed repeated staking and slicking over two days, working it damp each time. Third pass it finally broke and draped. Heavy leather now; will cut sole blanks from the densest section.

Alder-tanned rabbit-weight leather. Very thin. Fat liquor applied sparingly — too much and it goes floppy. Glass edge burnishing at light pressure only. Resulted in a fine, smooth panel. Cut into two glove blanks. Still need to punch and stitch them.
